name: 3rd Cousin
summary: Restaurant on Cortland Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Chef and owner Greg Lutes opened the restaurant in 2015.

name: A16
summary: Italian restaurant on Chestnut Street, San Francisco.
facts: Recognized as a Bib Gourmand by the MICHELIN Guide.
Serves rustic Italian cooking and a wide selection of pizzas.

name: Abrazo

facts: Opened in the former Zarzuela space on Hyde Street.
Run by chef Michael Pawlik and co-owner Amanda Banks Barker.

facts: Founded in 1998 and run by The Absinthe Group.

name: AK Subs
summary: Counter-service spot on 8th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has served sandwiches at 8th and Harrison since 1993.
Written up in SF Weekly's Cheap Eats and the Chronicle's Bargain Bites.

name: All Good Pizza
summary: Pizza restaurant on Jerrold Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Serves Neapolitan-style brick oven pizza in a 7,000-square-foot beer garden.

name: Anchor Oyster Bar
summary: Seafood restaurant on Castro Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has served oysters, clam chowder and sustainable seafood on Castro Street since 1977.

name: Andytown Coffee Roasters

name: Angler
summary: Seafood restaurant on The Embarcadero, San Francisco.

name: Arbor
summary: Restaurant on Hayes St, San Francisco.
facts: Serves burgers, sandwiches, salads and plant-based soft serve.

name: Arizmendi Bakery

name: Art's Cafe

name: Atwater Tavern
summary: Burger restaurant on Terry A. Francois Boulevard, San Francisco.

facts: Sells pasture-raised meat from small farms in Northern California.
Occupies a Bernal Heights shop that first opened nearly a century ago.

name: Avenues San Francisco
summary: Café on Taraval Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened by Eddie Choi on Taraval Street in 2018.
Serves musubi and a horchata cold brew made in-house.

name: Aziza
summary: Moroccan restaurant on Geary Boulevard, San Francisco.
facts: Aziza was the first Moroccan restaurant in the United States to earn a Michelin star.

name: b Patisserie

Leong was previously pastry chef at Gary Danko.

name: B Star

facts: Owned by Desmond Htunlin and Joycelyn Lee, who also own Burma Superstar and Eats.

name: Beach Chalet

facts: Designed by architect Willis Polk and opened in 1925 as a city-run restaurant with beach changing rooms.

Built in the Spanish Colonial Revival architecture style
Listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places

name: Beit Rima
summary: Arab restaurant on Church Street, San Francisco.

name: Bello Coffee & Tea
summary: Café on Diamond Street, San Francisco.
facts: Roasts its coffee on a zero-emission electric roaster.

name: Beretta
summary: Italian restaurant on Valencia Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 2008 and serves thin crust pizzas and Italian dishes.
Reopened in 2025 after a seven-week restoration with a new menu.

facts: Opened in 2018 inside the Minnesota Street Project, led by chef Heena Patel.

name: Birdsong
summary: Restaurant on Mission Street, San Francisco.
facts: Chef Christopher Bleidorn cooks meats and fish over live fire.

name: Biscuits & Blues

name: Breakfast at Tiffany's

name: Burma Superstar
summary: Asian restaurant on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened its original Clement Street location in 1992.
Has since opened additional locations in Alameda and Oakland.

name: Café Bunn Mi

name: Chouquet's

name: Cioppino's

name: Fillmore Bakeshop

name: Gary Danko

name: Hahdough

name: Jackson Fillmore Trattoria

facts: Opened in late 2016 to expand the Jane bakery program.

Largest Jane location, with a view of sourdough loaves coming out of the oven.

name: Java Beach Cafe

facts: Has been an Outer Sunset institution for 23 years as of 2016.
Also has a second location on Sloat Blvd.

name: Joe's Ice Cream
summary: Ice cream shop on Geary Boulevard, San Francisco.

name: Kahnfections

facts: Founder Judy Kahn opened the bakery in May 2017.

name: Kin Khao
summary: Thai restaurant on Cyril Magnin Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 2014 by chef-owner Pim Techamuanvivit.

name: Kitchen Istanbul
summary: Turkish restaurant on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: Named a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide USA.

name: Kokkari Estiatorio
summary: Greek restaurant on Jackson Street, San Francisco.
facts: Open in the Financial District since 1998.

name: La Ciccia

name: La Connessa

name: Loquat

name: Lucca Delicatessen

name: Mamahuhu
summary: Chinese restaurant on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: Chef Brandon Jew of Mister Jiu's opened it in 2020 as a homage to Chinese takeout.
Jew has since opened a second Mamahuhu location in San Francisco.

name: Mandalay
summary: Burmese restaurant on California Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened on February 4, 1984 and is the oldest running Burmese restaurant in San Francisco.
Named an America's Classic by the James Beard Foundation in 2024.
Serves tea leaf salad, paratha, mohinga and samusa soup.

name: Mario's Bohemian Cigar Store Cafe
summary: Café on Columbus Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 1971 when Mario and Liliana Crismani bought the Bohemian Cigar Store.
Serves oven-baked focaccia sandwiches on bread from Liguria Bakery.

name: Marlowe
summary: American restaurant on Brannan Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 2010 as a New American bistro.
Created by chef Jennifer Puccio and designer Ken Fulk.

name: Memphis Minnie's BBQ Joint
summary: Barbecue restaurant on Haight Street, San Francisco.
facts: Calls itself San Francisco's longest continuously running barbecue restaurant.
Has been at its Lower Haight location since 2000.
Smokes Southern-style barbecue slowly and serves pastrami only on Wednesdays.

name: Mission Blue
summary: Café on Leland Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: A cafe and gift shop serving Saint Frank's coffee.
Sells gifts from San Francisco artists and makers.
Its lavender latte uses lavender from the owner's garden.

name: Mission Bowling Club
summary: Burger restaurant on 17th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Anthony Myint of Mission Chinese Food was the food partner at opening.

name: Mission Rock Resort
summary: Seafood restaurant on Terry A. Francois Boulevard, San Francisco.
facts: Reopened in August 2012 under restaurateur Peter Osborne after Kelly's Mission Rock went bankrupt.
The site began in the early 1960s as a bait shop and burger joint.
Address: 817 Terry A. Francois Boulevard, San Francisco

name: Mister Jiu's
summary: Chinese restaurant on Waverly Place, San Francisco.
facts: Has held one Michelin star for nine consecutive years.
Housed in a landmark building that once held the Four Seas and Hang Far Low restaurants.

name: Mitchell's Ice Cream
summary: Ice cream shop on San Jose Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Brothers Larry and Jack Mitchell opened it on June 6, 1953.
In the early 1960s it was the first to introduce mango ice cream to the Bay Area.
Still owned and operated by the Mitchell family.
Address: 688 San Jose Avenue, San Francisco

name: Moscow & Tbilisi Bakery Store
summary: Bakery on Geary Boulevard, San Francisco.
facts: Sells Russian and Georgian baked goods, including cheese blintzes and poppy seed rolls.
Chebureki, deep-fried turnovers filled with ground beef, are a staple.

name: Neighbor's Corner
summary: Café on Douglass St, San Francisco.
facts: A cafe in residential Eureka Valley serving espresso drinks and breakfast sandwiches.
The drink menu leans toward Japanese-influenced coffee, including hojicha lattes and matcha.

name: Nute's
summary: Japanese restaurant on Cortland Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Serves Japanese and Thai noodles, including khao soi and ramen.
Its tonkotsu ramen is flavored with roasted black garlic oil.
Serves Japanese food, plus noodles and ramen

name: Octavia
summary: Restaurant on Octavia Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 2015 as the second restaurant from chef-owner Melissa Perello.
Was awarded a Michelin star within its first year of business.

name: Okane
summary: Sushi restaurant on Townsend Street, San Francisco.
facts: Named a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide USA.
Serves Japanese izakaya dishes such as cod marinated in sake lees.

name: Old Skool Cafe
summary: Café on Mendell Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has trained and employed at-risk and formerly incarcerated youth for more than 20 years.
Runs as a 1920s-themed supper club with live jazz.

name: On the Bridge
summary: Japanese restaurant on Webster Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves okonomiyaki pizza and 23 types of Japanese pasta.
Sits on the bridge between Japantown East and West.

name: Original Joe's
summary: Italian restaurant on Union Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 1937 as a 14-stool counter in the Tenderloin.
Reopened in North Beach in 2012 after a 2007 fire at the original site.
Serves Italian food, plus burgers and pasta

name: Outerlands
summary: American restaurant on Judah Street, San Francisco.
facts: Recognized as a Bib Gourmand by the MICHELIN Guide.
Known for house-baked sourdough bread and fried mortadella sandwiches.

https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Speci.author: San Francisco Planning Department from United States

name: Pagan
summary: Burmese restaurant on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves Burmese and Thai classics in a sit-down space.
Named after the city of Pagan in Burma.

name: Panadería La Mejor
summary: Bakery on 24th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Carmen Elias opened the Mexican bakery in 1993 after retiring from Bank of America.
Named a San Francisco legacy business in 2024.
The storefront window art is hand painted each month by a local artist.

name: Paper Son Coffee - FiDi
summary: Café on 2nd Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves locally roasted coffee and Asian American-inspired drinks.
The name honors the paper son immigration history of the founder's family.

name: Parachute
summary: Café in San Francisco.
facts: Opened at the Ferry Building on September 4, 2025.
Founded by Alex Hong and Joel Wilkerson of Michelin-starred Sorrel, with head baker Nasir Armar.

name: Perry's
summary: Restaurant on Union Street, San Francisco.
facts: Perry Butler opened it in August 1969 as a place for burgers and wine.
Marked its 50th anniversary on Union Street in 2019.

name: Pinhole Coffee
summary: Café on Cortland Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: A multi-roaster cafe founded by JoEllen Depakakibo.
Opened in 2014 on Cortland Avenue in Bernal Heights.

name: Pizzetta 211
summary: Pizza restaurant on 23rd Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Serves thin-crust pizzettas on a menu that changes every two weeks.
Opened in 1999 by Ria Ramsey and Sher Rogat, neither formally trained as chefs.

name: Plow
summary: Regional restaurant on 18th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 2010 by Joel Bleskacek and Maxine Siu, who met at Oliveto in Oakland.
Built out a vacant architect studio in Potrero Hill with local contractors and Bay Area materials.

name: PLS on Post
summary: Burger restaurant on Post Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in late August 2022 by Sage Hospitality Group on the ground floor of Hotel Zeppelin.
The name stands for peace, love, and soul, honoring 1960s San Francisco counterculture.

name: Polly Ann Ice Cream
summary: Ice cream shop on Noriega Street, San Francisco.
facts: An Outer Sunset ice cream parlor since 1955.
Known for Asian-inspired flavors and featured on Anthony Bourdain's TV show.

name: Pork Store Cafe
summary: American restaurant on Haight Street, San Francisco.
facts: Calls itself San Francisco's original breakfast spot, serving since 1916.
Specializes in American comfort food for breakfast and lunch.
Serves American food, plus coffee and breakfast
hours: Mon–Wed 8am–3:30pm; Thu 8am–10pm; Fri 8am–midnight; Sat 12am–1:30am; Sat 8am–10pm; Sun 8am–7pm

name: Progress
summary: American restaurant on Fillmore Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves Californian shared plates in a two-story space with skylights.
Cooks Liberty Farms duck with peanut fried rice.

name: Prubechu
summary: Guamanian restaurant on Mission Street, San Francisco.
facts: Started in 2014 by chef Shawn Naputi and business partner Shawn Camacho, both raised on Guam.
Serves classic flavors from Guam and the Mariana Islands.
Described in 2020 as San Francisco's only Chamorro restaurant.

name: Quince
summary: Restaurant on Pacific Ave, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 2003 and run by Michael and Lindsay Tusk.
Serves nightly-changing tasting menus built on a partnership with Fresh Run Farm in Bolinas.

name: R & G Lounge
summary: Chinese restaurant on Kearny Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1985 as a one-story restaurant in a basement.
Has since grown to three dining floors.

name: Red Blossom Tea Company
summary: Tea shop on Grant Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Sources single-origin teas directly from farmers in China and Taiwan.

name: Red Window
summary: Restaurant on Columbus Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Serves Spanish-style tapas and pintxos with low-proof cocktails built on vermouth, amaro and sherry.
Run by bar manager Elmer Mejicanos and chef Adam Rosenblum, a Causwells alum.
hours: Tue–Thu 5pm–10pm; Fri, Sat 10am–11pm; Sun 10am–8pm; Mon closed

name: Rich Table
summary: Italian restaurant on Gough Street, San Francisco.
facts: Led by chefs Evan and Sarah Rich.
Has a sister restaurant, RT Bistro, on Oak Street.

name: Rose's Café
summary: Italian restaurant on Union Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has operated in Cow Hollow since 1997.
Ava Rosemary Nicolai took ownership of Rose's Cafe and sister restaurant Terzo in December 2025.
Cooks Italian-rooted dishes with seasonal Northern California ingredients.

name: RT Bistro
summary: American restaurant on Oak Street, San Francisco.
facts: Sister restaurant to Rich Table from chefs Evan and Sarah Rich.
Serves California bistro cooking with a la carte and chef's menu options.

name: Saltwater Bakeshop
summary: Bakery on Howard Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened its first permanent storefront on Howard St in May 2026 after years at farmers markets.
Owner Brittany Dunn Holden bakes sourdough, croissants and pastries.

name: San Ho Won
summary: Korean, charcoal BBQ restaurant.
facts: Holds one Michelin star in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide USA.
Korean restaurant with chefs Corey Lee and Jeong-In Hwang.

name: San Tung
summary: Chinese restaurant on Irving Street, San Francisco.
facts: Established in 1986 and serves Northern Style Chinese cooking.
Specializes in spicy chicken wings, dumplings and noodles.

name: Schroeder's Restaurant
summary: German restaurant on Front Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 1893 by Henry Schroeder; rebuilt after the 1906 fire at Front Street.
Called the oldest and largest German restaurant on the West Coast.
Admitted only men at lunch until the 1970s.

name: Scoma's
summary: Seafood restaurant in San Francisco.
facts: Brothers Albert and Joseph Scoma opened it on Pier 47 in May 1965.
It started by taking over a six-stool coffee shop that served fishermen.
Jones Alley was renamed Al Scoma Way, with a dedication in 2002.

name: Sears Fine Food
summary: Pancake restaurant on Powell Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 1938 by Hilbur and Ben Sears on Powell Street near Union Square.
Known for its 18 Swedish pancakes made from the Sears family recipe.
Reopened in August 2004 after closing in 2003.

name: Sextant Coffee Roasters
summary: Café on Folsom Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded by Kinani Ahmed, a first-generation Ethiopian.
Works directly with farmers across Ethiopia, Kenya and Colombia.

name: Sheba Piano Lounge
summary: Ethiopian restaurant on Fillmore Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 2006 in the Fillmore District by chef Net Alemayehu.
Serves Ethiopian dishes alongside live music.
A wall in the dining room is built to resemble the Bet Giorgis church in Lalibela.

name: Simple Pleasures Cafe
summary: Café on Balboa Street, San Francisco.
facts: Sandy Berger opened it in 1978 as a bohemian coffee shop.
Ahmed Riad bought it in 1994 and still owns it.

name: Smitten
summary: Ice cream shop on Valencia Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founder Robyn Sue Fisher invented the Brrr machine, which makes ice cream to order with liquid nitrogen.
Fisher started in 2009 as a street cart vendor with a prototype machine on a Radio Flyer wagon.
The Valencia Street shop reopened in November 2023 after a vandalism closure.

name: Snowbird Coffee
summary: Café on 9th Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in fall 2014 between Judah and Irving.
Serves cafe bombons, two espresso shots over condensed milk.

name: Sorella
summary: Restaurant on Polk Street, San Francisco.
facts: Sister restaurant to Acquerello, serving Californian cooking by way of Northern Italy.
House-made pastas anchor the menu, with cicchetti and cocktails at the bar.

name: Sorrel
summary: Californian restaurant on Sacramento Street, San Francisco.
facts: Chef Alexander Hong trained at Quince and serves contemporary Italian cooking.
A rooftop garden supplies herbs, edible flowers and seasonal vegetables.
Serves Italian food, plus californian and modern

name: Sotto Mare
summary: Oysteria and seafood.
facts: The building dates to 1919 and was a winery and cigar store during Prohibition.
Opened as Sotto Mare Oysteria & Seafood on March 17, 2007.
The Azzolino family bought the restaurant in 2014.

name: SSAL
summary: Korean restaurant on Polk Street, San Francisco.
facts: Holds one Michelin star in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide USA.
Hyunyoung and Junsoo Bae run this Korean tasting menu restaurant.

name: St Francis Fountain
summary: Old San Francisco diner with many vegan options.
facts: Founded in 1918 by James Christakes, an immigrant from Sparta, Greece.
It is the oldest continuously operating business on 24th Street.
Still sells vintage candies from its original 1920s candy case.

name: Starbelly
summary: Restaurant on 16th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 2009 by Deborah Blum and Adriano Paganini, who also run Beretta.
Took over the former Asquew Grill space.

name: State Bird Provisions
summary: American restaurant on Fillmore Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves seasonal California dishes from carts in a dim sum style.

name: Suppenküche
summary: German restaurant on Laguna Street, San Francisco.

name: Sweet Maple
summary: Breakfast restaurant on Sutter Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves American breakfast and brunch with an Asian influence, including Millionaire's Bacon.

name: Swensen's Ice Cream
summary: Café on Hyde Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1948 by Earle Swensen at the corner of Union and Hyde.
Current owner Richard Campana started working there at age fifteen.

name: Taqueria Cancun
summary: Mexican restaurant on Mission Street, San Francisco.
facts: First opened in 1991 on Market Street.
Started by two alumni of El Farolito.

name: Telescope Coffee
summary: Café on 6th St, San Francisco.
facts: Moved from 451 9th St to a larger space on 6th St in 2023.
Serves Vietnamese coffee brewed with a phin filter.

name: Thanh Long
summary: Vietnamese restaurant on Judah Street, San Francisco.
facts: Established in 1971 as a family-run restaurant on Judah Street.
Became the city's first Vietnamese restaurant.
Garlic noodles with tiger prawns and whole-roasted Dungeness crab first came to life here.

name: The Brazen Head
summary: Restaurant on Buchanan Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves a continental menu with escargot, French onion soup and a pepper steak.
Describes itself as a talking bar in the heart of Cow Hollow.
Has served over three generations of patrons.

name: The Game Parlour
summary: Café on Irving Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 2018 as San Francisco's first board game cafe.
Pairs food with tabletop games for people of all ages.

name: The Garden Court
summary: Restaurant on New Montgomery St, San Francisco.
facts: Covered by a stained glass dome with more than 70,000 pieces of colored glass.
The Palace Hotel opened on its present site on December 19, 1909.
Address: 2 New Montgomery St, San Francisco

name: The Mill
summary: Café on Divisadero Street, San Francisco.
facts: Is a joint venture of Four Barrel Coffee and Josey Baker Bread, which began in 2010.

name: The Sentinel
summary: Sandwich restaurant on New Montgomery Street, San Francisco.
facts: Established in 2008 by chef Dennis Leary.
Occupies an old cigar shop across from the Palace Hotel.
Address: 37 New Montgomery Street, San Francisco

name: The Velo Rouge Cafe
summary: Café on Arguello Boulevard, San Francisco.
facts: A bike-themed cafe a block from the Arguello entrance to Golden Gate Park.
Serves breakfast burritos, bagels and a tuna melt panini.

name: Tommaso's Ristorante Italiano
summary: Italian restaurant on Kearny Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1935 as Lupo's by the Cantalupo family from Naples.
Awarded San Francisco Legacy Business status in 2017.

name: Tommy’s Mexican Restaurant
summary: Mexican restaurant on Geary Boulevard, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1965 by Tommy and Elmy Bermejo; their son Julio now runs it.
Serves only 100% agave tequila, with a collection of 300+ brands.
The Tommy's Margarita was created here and swaps sour mix for fresh lime and agave syrup.

name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
summary: Pizza restaurant on Stockton Street, San Francisco.
facts: Ranked third among U.S. pizzerias by 50 Top Pizza in 2025.

name: Toy Boat Dessert Café
summary: Restaurant on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: Jesse Fink opened it in 1982 with his girlfriend at the time, Roberta.
The cafe had vintage toys and a 1950s mechanical horse named Butterscotch that kids could ride.
Reopened in June 2025 as Toy Boat by Jane, with baked goods from Jane.

name: Trattoria Contadina
summary: Italian restaurant on Mason St, San Francisco.
facts: Vincent Correnti opened it in 1984; three generations of his family have owned it.
Joined the San Francisco Legacy Business Registry on May 23, 2022.

name: Trestle
summary: Restaurant on Jackson Street, San Francisco.
facts: Named a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide USA.
Serves a prix fixe Californian menu with two seasonal options per course.

name: Tú Lan
summary: Vietnamese restaurant on 6th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened around 1976 as one of the first Vietnamese restaurants in San Francisco.
Founded by Thao Nguyen and his sister Thu Hang Nguyen.
Joined the San Francisco Legacy Business Registry in December 2021.

name: um.ma
summary: Japanese restaurant on 9th Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Chef Chris Oh opened Um.ma in 2019 as a homage to his mother's Korean cooking.
Makes its own kimchi and serves Korean fried chicken.
hours: Mon 5pm–9pm; Tue closed; Wed–Thu 11am–2pm; Wed–Thu 5pm–9pm; Fri–Sat 11am–10pm; Sun 11am–9pm

name: Victoria Pastry Company
summary: Bakery on Filbert Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 1914 by seven bakers who combined four competing North Beach bakeries.
Moved to Filbert Street in 2012 after nearly 100 years at Stockton and Vallejo.

name: Vive La Tarte
summary: Café on 24th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded by self-taught baker Julie Vandermeersch and her husband Arnaud Goethals.
Created the tacro, a croissant folded and filled like a taco.

name: Wako
summary: Japanese restaurant on Clement St, San Francisco.
facts: Awarded one Michelin star in the 2019 MICHELIN Guide California.
Offers two omakase options: a sushi tasting menu and a full omakase.

name: Warming Hut
summary: Café on Marine Drive, San Francisco.
facts: Housed in a historic U.S. Engineer Storehouse reborn as a park store in 2001.
Sells coffee, hot chocolate, packaged snacks, park books and clothing.

name: Wayfare Tavern
summary: Restaurant on Pine Street, San Francisco.
facts: Chef Tyler Florence moved it here in spring 2025 after 14 years on Sacramento Street.
The menu is American food inspired by local cuisine of the early 1900s.

name: Wing Lee Bakery
summary: Bakery on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: Chef Brandon Jew of Mister Jiu's goes here for a dumpling his grandmother used to make.
Jew opened Mamahuhu two doors down in 2020.

name: Wooly Pig
summary: Café on 3rd Street, San Francisco.
facts: Held the grand opening of its Dogpatch cafe in June 2018.
Relocated to Dogpatch from the Inner Sunset.

name: Yank Sing
summary: Chinese restaurant on Spear Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has been a San Francisco dim sum restaurant since 1958.
A third-generation, family-owned restaurant serving dim sum from pushcarts.

name: Yuet Lee Seafood Restaurant
summary: Chinese restaurant on Stockton St, San Francisco.
facts: Cantonese seafood restaurant open since the 1970s.
Serves whole steamed fish, salt and pepper prawns and clams in black bean sauce.

name: Z & Y Restaurant
summary: Chinese restaurant on Jackson Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves Sichuan cooking led by owner and executive chef Lijun Han.
Dishes include tea-smoked duck and fish filet in chili oil.

name: Zazie
summary: French restaurant on Cole Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in Cole Valley in 1992 by Catherine Opoix.
Named for the main character of Louis Malle's film Zazie dans le Metro.
Jennifer Piallat bought the restaurant in 2005 and sold it to three employees in 2020.
